title: Implication of Allianz Insurance's Proposed Acquisition of Income Insurance on Affordable Insurance for Singaporeans and Government's Support of Co-operatives
what_it_is: Implication of Allianz Insurance's Proposed Acquisition of Income Insurance on Affordable Insurance for Singaporeans and Government's Support of Co-operatives

sections.label: Income Insurance Allianz sale questions
sections.summary: MPs asked whether the sale of NTUC Enterprise's 51% stake in Income Insurance to Allianz affects affordability, availability and Income's social mission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) whether NTUC Enterprise's sale of its 51% stake in Income Insurance Ltd to a foreign insurance company will impact affordability and availability of essential insurance products to the broad mass consumers and small enterprise segment in the long term; and (b) whether there is social value for NTUC Enterprise to retain its controlling stake in Income Insurance Ltd so that the provision of insurance services remains inclusive and accessible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth with the proposed majority stake acquisition of Income Insurance Ltd by Allianz Insurance, how will the Government continue to support the co-operative movement in providing Singaporeans with affordable essential goods and services in the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth regarding the potential acquisition of a majority stake in Income Insurance Ltd by Allianz Insurance, whether the Government will work with the National Trades Union Congress to assess the potential impact on (i) insurance coverage for lower-income groups and workers and (ii) Income Insurance Ltd's original social mission if it is acquired by a foreign-listed profit-driven commercial entity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) whether MAS can provide an update on the sale of Income Insurance Ltd to Allianz Insurance, a foreign for-profit insurer; (b) what steps can MAS take to ensure that Income Insurance Ltd continues to provide accessible insurance products to Singapore citizens; and (c) whether companies set up with a social purpose and has performed a critical role in keeping prices affordable for Singaporeans should be designated by legislation as critical entities which require approval from the Government for ownership or control changes.

sections.label: CCF grants to co-ops
sections.summary: CCF disbursed about $2.7 million in grants to co-ops over the last five years, including startup funding and grants for emerging threats, risks and needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: CCF disbursed about $2.7 million in grants to our co-ops over the last five years, including startup funding for new co-ops and grants that co-ops can use to address their emerging threats, risks and needs.

sections.label: Income corporatisation and capital buffers
sections.summary: Income's capital buffers came under pressure, so it sought to corporatise in 2022; RCS said members should decide, and members voted overwhelmingly in favour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The current situation for Income cannot be sustained and Income's capital buffers have repeatedly come under pressure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: But NTUC Enterprise cannot do this on its own.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: That is why Income sought to corporatise in 2022, so that it could consider more options to access more capital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: When this was surfaced to the Registry of Co-operative Societies (RCS), RCS had advised all parties that this was a matter for NTUC Income and its members to collectively determine and resolve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Eventually, members voted overwhelmingly in favour of corporatisation.

sections.label: Allianz commitments and SIRA safeguards
sections.summary: Allianz committed to honour existing policies, join national insurance programmes and continue charity commitments; NTUC and Income assured affordable premiums; SIRA safeguards were introduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Allianz has committed to honour Income's existing policies; participate in national insurance programmes; and continue its charity commitments, including the pledge of $100 million over 10 years from 2021 to provide social mobility among the lower-income and support the well-being of seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: NTUC and Income have also given their assurance to keep premiums affordable for Income's low-cost schemes for its members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: On Mr Saktiandi Supaat's question, the Government has introduced the Significant Investments Review Act, or SIRA, safeguards, to designate entities that provide a critical function to national security interests.

sections.label: NTUC and Allianz premium assurances
sections.summary: NTUC and Allianz assured they will continue NTUC Gift and Income Insurance's LUV Life Insurance schemes and keep premiums affordable, especially for low-income policyholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In this new proposed deal, NTUC as well as Allianz has made assurances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I have outlined these assurances in NTUC's statement, that it will continue with the two schemes, NTUC Gift and Income Insurance's "LUV Life Insurance", and to keep these premiums affordable for policyholders, especially for the low-income segments.

sections.label: Allianz policy and pledge assurance
sections.summary: Allianz said the proposed deal will not affect current policies and it will continue the pledge to disburse $100 million over 10 years from 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: On its part, Allianz has also said that the proposed deal will not affect the current policy and they will continue to uphold the pledge to disburse the $100 million over 10 years, from 2021.

sections.label: Allianz written commitment question
sections.summary: A question asks whether Allianz has given a written commitment to allow Income to continue its social mission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: My first question is, although he has touched on the assurances that Allianz has given for the deal, but I would still like to ask whether Allianz has given a commitment in writing to allow Income to continue its social mission.

sections.label: Confusion over Income's status
sections.summary: Singaporeans are confused because Mr Andrew Yeo said corporatised Income remains an NTUC social enterprise while Mr Lim Boon Heng implied it is a private enterprise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Because Singaporeans are confused that NTUC Income's CEO, Mr Andrew Yeo, had stated two years ago, that the corporatised Income will remain an NTUC social enterprise, while NTUC Enterprise Chairman, Mr Lim Boon Heng, has just implied in a recent interview that Income should be treated as a private enterprise and thus, we should not interfere in this transaction.

sections.label: Allianz commitments to Income
sections.summary: NTUC's statement says Allianz is committed to honouring Income's existing policies, national insurance programmes, charity commitments and a $100 million pledge over 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And then this other question, with regard to the social mission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I have explained and in NTUC's statement, it has already said that Allianz is committed to honouring Income's existing policies, participating in national insurance programmes, continuing its charity commitments, also including the pledge of $100 million over 10 years.

sections.label: NTUC Enterprise capital injections
sections.summary: Other insurers faced crises and challenges adhering to capital adequacy and solvency standards, so NTUC Enterprise made publicly known capital injections of up to about $630 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And in fact, if you think about the insurance industry, there are also other insurance companies and financial institutions who have gone through repeated financial crises – be it the Asian Financial Crisis, the Global Financial Crisis, SARS or the COVID-19 pandemic that has just passed – where they have been unable, for example, or have faced challenges to adhere to capital adequacy ratios and solvency standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And therefore, NTUC Enterprise had to put in capital injections of up to, it is publicly known, about up to $630 million.

sections.label: Allianz alignment with NTUC Income
sections.summary: After trying, and cognisant of ground challenges, they said Allianz has the best alignment with NTUC Income, with a long-term view to protect Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And make no mistake about that, they have tried, which is an answer to many of these questions that are floating on the ground.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: But after having tried so many of this and being cognisant of the fact of the challenges on the ground, they said "Allianz has the best alignment with NTUC Income." What is the purpose for that then?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: It is not just to address all of the challenges which I have lined up, the capital side and the competitive side, but it is also one central reason why they do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: That is a long-term view to protect Singaporeans for the long term.

sections.label: Goh Keng Swee on co-ops
sections.summary: Dr Goh Keng Swee stressed that co-ops must be competitive, financially sustainable and receive no privileged treatment from Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Dr Goh Keng Swee firmly stressed the key principles for co-ops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: He said that co-ops must be competitive, it must be financially sustainable, receiving no privileged treatment from Government.

sections.label: NTUC COVID-19 worker support
sections.summary: During COVID-19 the Job Security Council was a lifeline for workers, and NTUC and its social enterprises have contributed over $300 million to charity programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Then, during COVID-19, it was a lifeline for workers, with the Job Security Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And throughout the years, throughout the decades, NTUC and the NTUC social enterprises have contributed over $300 million to various charity programmes.

sections.label: NTUC Enterprise Allianz deal structure
sections.summary: The deal structure gives NTUC Enterprise up to 49% and Allianz 51%, with NTUC Enterprise having a significant say in the new entity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: And not just for this case, but future cases, for changes or acquisition of co-ops going forward as well, in terms of the legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: But in public, the structure of the deal is that NTUC Enterprise, up to 49%, and it is a significant shareholding, and Allianz, 51%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: So, NTUC Enterprise will have a significant say in how this proposed new entity will run and they have already publicly made very clear statements, on both sides, both NTUC Enterprise, Income, as well as Allianz, about what they will do should this deal progress.
